facets.title: Makeup Subsystem
facets.definition: Which major part of the makeup look is currently being worked on (complexion, brows, eyes, lashes, lips, etc.).
guidelines: Label based on the primary work area being actively manipulated during that span (what the demonstrator is applying/refining), not what is being discussed.
If a step explicitly covers two areas, choose the dominant/longer or higher-attention area; if truly split, segment into two spans where the focus changes.
Change the label when the tutorial clearly shifts to working on a different facial subsystem (e.g., leaves base products and begins eye construction).

vocabulary.label: cheeks (blush/contour/highlight)
vocabulary.definition: Application, placement, or blending of cheek-area color and sculpting products—including blush, bronzer/contour, nose/face sculpting, and cheek highlighter—to add color, warmth, shape, or illumination. This label covers adjustments to placement, intensity, and finish on the cheek/cheekbone area and is distinct from complexion/base (foundation/concealer/powder) and from eye, brow, lash, or lip work.

facets.title: Routine Phase
facets.definition: The step’s position in the overall makeup workflow (prepping, building base, constructing features, finishing/locking, or later touch-ups).
guidelines: Use the tutorial’s procedural order and explicit transitions (e.g., 'before foundation', 'now to set', 'to finish') to assign phase.
If the creator removes makeup/reset to start a new look, label that span as Removal/Reset until base prep/build restarts.
Touch-ups/redo segments are labeled only when the tutorial is revisiting earlier areas to refresh or correct wear, not when initially applying.

vocabulary.label: prep
vocabulary.definition: Procedures performed before applying complexion or feature products to prepare the skin/eyes (cleansing, moisturizing, exfoliating, priming, eye primer, and any pre-coverage color-correction) — everything done prior to building the base.

vocabulary.label: base build
vocabulary.definition: Applying and blending complexion coverage and correction products to establish the skin base prior to setting (foundation, concealer, correctors, tinted moisturizers, cream contour/highlight applied as part of the base).

vocabulary.label: feature construction
vocabulary.definition: Building and defining facial features using makeup products after the base is laid down (eyeshadow layering and blending, brow filling/shaping, eyeliner, mascara applied as product, lip color application, product-based contouring). Excludes attachable or wearable items (e.g., false lashes, contacts, prosthetics) which are labeled under Accessory Application.

vocabulary.label: finish/lock-in
vocabulary.definition: Setting, locking, and finalizing steps performed to increase longevity and harmonize the completed look immediately before the tutorial ends (setting powders/sprays, final blending/balancing, finishing touches intended as finalization rather than later refresh).

vocabulary.label: touch-up/refresh
vocabulary.definition: Revisits after initial application intended to refresh, correct wear, intensify, or adapt the look (day-to-night refreshes, localized corrections) — applied only when the creator is returning to previously completed areas rather than performing initial application.

vocabulary.label: removal/reset
vocabulary.definition: Removing makeup and/or cleansing to fully reset the face to a bare state, or otherwise stripping a prior look to begin a new base-prep/build sequence.

vocabulary.label: accessory application
vocabulary.definition: Applying attachable or wearable enhancements that complete the look but are not product-based feature construction (inserting colored contact lenses, applying false/strip lashes, lash extensions adhesive work, stick-on gems/crystals, prosthetic pieces, decorative accessories). This phase is distinct from feature construction and from finish/setting steps.

facets.title: Material State
facets.definition: The primary physical state/handling form of the product (or non-product step) being manipulated in the moment.
guidelines: Label by the main material being worked with during the step; if two states are used sequentially (e.g., curl then mascara), segment if the tutorial clearly treats them as separate actions; otherwise label by the dominant action.
Treat gel/liquid liners, concealers, foundations, primers, mascara, and gloss as Wet/Cream-Liquid.
Treat loose/pressed setting powder, eyeshadow, blush/bronzer/highlighter powders as Dry/Powder.
Treat pencils, sticks, and bullet lipsticks as Solid/Stick-Pencil when that format is central.

vocabulary.label: dry/powder
vocabulary.definition: Loose or pressed powder products applied by sweeping, pressing, or buffing (e.g., setting powder, pressed/loose eyeshadow, powder blush/bronzer/highlighter).

vocabulary.label: wet/cream-liquid
vocabulary.definition: Liquid, cream, or gel products that are applied and typically blended or allowed to dry/set (e.g., liquid foundation, cream concealer, gel liner, mascara, gloss).

vocabulary.label: solid/stick-pencil
vocabulary.definition: Solid-format products applied by direct drawing or swatching (pencils, sticks, bullet lipsticks, solid crayons/sticks where the solid form is central).

vocabulary.label: accessory/tool-only
vocabulary.definition: Steps where no cosmetic product is deposited and the primary action is mechanical or tool-focused (e.g., lash curler-only, contact insertion, tool placement/manipulation).

vocabulary.label: removal solvent
vocabulary.definition: Remover or cleansing liquids/solutions used to dissolve and wipe away makeup or adhesive (e.g., micellar water, oil cleansers, makeup remover).

vocabulary.label: loose glitter/pigment
vocabulary.definition: Loose reflective glitter or large-particle pigments applied as free particulates—often patted on with an adhesive/tack medium and handled differently from typical powder eyeshadows due to fallout and adhesion needs.

facets.title: Primary Tool Class
facets.definition: The main applicator/tool category used to perform the step’s core action.
guidelines: Label based on the tool that performs the primary manipulation (depositing/blending/pressing/drawing).
If multiple tools are used but one is clearly the main action driver, choose that; if two tools are used in clearly separate consecutive actions, segment at the tool change when feasible.
Classify small precision brushes used for liner/crease/brow carving as Eye/Brow Detail Brush; classify large fluffy/face brushes as Face Brush.

vocabulary.label: fingers/hands
vocabulary.definition: Direct application using fingertips or whole hands as the primary applicator for depositing, blending, or pressing product.

vocabulary.label: sponge/puff
vocabulary.definition: Compressible applicator (beauty sponge, blending sponge, powder puff) used to press, blend, or sheer product onto skin.

vocabulary.label: face brush
vocabulary.definition: Larger brushes used for complexion work (foundation, powder, bronzer, blush, finishing) that perform the main depositing or blending action.

vocabulary.label: eye/brow detail brush
vocabulary.definition: Small precision brushes used for eye or brow detail (liner, crease, shader, brow carving) where a narrow brush drives the primary manipulation.

vocabulary.label: lash tools
vocabulary.definition: Tools specifically for lashes (eyelash curler, mascara wand/spoolie) that perform the primary action on lashes.

vocabulary.label: cotton pad/q-tip
vocabulary.definition: Disposable cotton implements (cotton pad, cotton bud/q-tip) used primarily for smudging, cleanup, removal, or precision wiping.

vocabulary.label: no hand tool (accessory placement)
vocabulary.definition: Steps that primarily place or attach an accessory (e.g., false lashes, stickers) rather than using a hand-held applicator to apply or blend cosmetics.

vocabulary.label: spray/mist applicator
vocabulary.definition: Handheld pump, aerosol, or airbrush-style sprayer that deposits product as a fine mist across the face and is the primary applicator for that step.

vocabulary.label: pencil/liner
vocabulary.definition: Rigid or semi-rigid pencil/crayon-style applicators (wood or automatic pencils, kohl, crayon) used to draw or define precise lines (eye, lip, brow) as the main tool.

vocabulary.label: pen/brush-tip liner
vocabulary.definition: Felt-tip, brush-tip, or thin brush-style pen applicators (liquid eyeliner pens, brush-tip liners) used as the primary tool for precise, sharp lines or wings.

vocabulary.label: product applicator
vocabulary.definition: Built-in product applicators integrated into the product housing (doe-foot/wand, gloss/lip wands, stick/bullet/tube formats) used to deposit or spread product directly without a separate hand tool.

facets.title: Look occasion
facets.definition: The intended occasion/intensity context of the current look segment (how bold/elevated the overall makeup goal is at that time).
guidelines: Label based on the segment goal stated/implicit in the tutorial (e.g., “nude/everyday,” “night/cabaret/glam,” or “day-to-night”).
Do not infer from a single product alone; use the surrounding segment framing (e.g., daytime version vs nighttime version vs upgrade).
If the tutorial explicitly transitions from day to night without removing makeup, label the upgrade segment as Day-to-Night Upgrade.

vocabulary.label: everyday/nude
vocabulary.definition: Natural, low-intensity, wearable makeup intended primarily for daytime or everyday contexts; focuses on subtle enhancement rather than bold or performance-driven techniques.

vocabulary.label: dramatic/night glam
vocabulary.definition: High-intensity, evening or performance-oriented makeup with bolder definition, stronger contrast, and more pronounced finishes suited for nights out or glam occasions.

vocabulary.label: day-to-night upgrade
vocabulary.definition: A transition segment that intensifies or elevates an existing daytime look for evening use without fully removing or rebuilding the base makeup.

vocabulary.label: editorial/photoshoot
vocabulary.definition: A camera-focused, high-impact creative look intended for photoshoots, video, or editorial contexts; typically uses bolder pigments, graphic techniques, and finishing choices that are optimized to read on camera and may be more stylized than standard night glam.

facets.title: Workflow phase
facets.definition: The step’s role in the build-refine-finish structure of the current makeup look (including optional embellishments).
guidelines: Use surrounding sequence cues: early mapping/building = Core Application; ‘add more,’ ‘increase definition,’ ‘again,’ or ‘reapply to intensify’ = Enhancement/Intensify; ‘complete/finish the look’ or final detailing passes = Finishing/Last Pass; explicitly presented as skippable = Optional Add-on.
Finishing/Last Pass should be reserved for late-stage steps after the main eyes/face/lips have been established.
If a step repeats an earlier product specifically to make it stronger for a new context (e.g., night), label Enhancement/Intensify rather than Finishing.

vocabulary.label: core application
vocabulary.definition: Primary build steps that establish the main components, color, and shape of the current look (early-stage actions that create the base of eyes/face/lips).

vocabulary.label: enhancement/intensify
vocabulary.definition: Steps that increase impact, definition, or longevity of an already-established look — often repeat or layer earlier products to make them stronger or more defined.

vocabulary.label: finishing/last pass
vocabulary.definition: Late-stage steps performed after major features are established that finalize, balance, or add last detailing to complete the look.

vocabulary.label: optional add-on
vocabulary.definition: A skippable embellishment or extra detail that is not required to complete the intended look (presented as optional or clearly nonessential).

vocabulary.label: preparatory/priming
vocabulary.definition: Setup actions performed before the main build that affect technique or outcomes but do not primarily add visible color/shape (e.g., skin priming/moisturizing, mixing primer/illuminator, curling lashes, pressing brightening/setting powder to catch fallout).

vocabulary.label: cleanse/reset between looks
vocabulary.definition: Transitional actions that remove existing makeup and restore a clean base so a new look can be started; treated as outside the build/refine/finish flow of the current look.

facets.title: Look iteration
facets.definition: Whether the current segment is (a) a continuous single-look application, (b) a new look after removing/resetting prior makeup, or (c) a day-to-night modification of an existing look.
guidelines: Label “Single Look (continuous)” when the routine proceeds forward without a remover/reset and without an explicit day-to-night modification segment.

Label “Second Look after Reset” starting when makeup is removed/clean slate is created and the next look begins (e.g., remover used, brows redone for the next look), ending before any subsequent reset.
Label “Day-to-Night Transition” starting at explicit refresh/intensify steps that modify the daytime makeup for evening (often includes touch-up concealer/powder and intensifying liner/lips).

vocabulary.label: single look (continuous)
vocabulary.definition: A single makeup look built continuously on the same base without a full removal/reset and without an explicit day-to-night intensification; minor touch-ups that do not restart the routine are allowed.

vocabulary.label: second look after reset
vocabulary.definition: A new, distinct look that begins after prior makeup has been removed or the face has been otherwise reset (e.g., remover used, base/skin re-cleansed, brows redone), with the segment ending before any subsequent reset.

vocabulary.label: day-to-night transition
vocabulary.definition: An explicit refresh or intensification of an existing daytime look for evening wear without fully removing makeup (commonly includes touch-up concealer/powder and intensifying liner, eyeshadow, or lip color).

facets.title: Step Function
facets.definition: The main procedural role the step serves in constructing the eye look, independent of the specific shade name.
guidelines: Label by the step’s primary goal in the sequence (what it accomplishes in the look), not by the tool.
Use preceding/following cues: mapping/base → transition build → lid placement → refinement/edge diffusion → deepening/dimension → liner/lashes.
If the step both deposits and blends, choose the dominant intent (e.g., ‘press onto lid’ = lid placement even if minor blending occurs).
When a step is explicitly about softening/cleaning borders, label as edge diffusion/refinement even if it uses the same color.

vocabulary.label: mapping / base
vocabulary.definition: Preparing the eye canvas or mapping the eye shape: includes applying a base/primer or lightly sketching crease and outer-eye boundaries to create an even surface and guide later pigment placement.

vocabulary.label: cut-crease definition
vocabulary.definition: Creating or reinforcing a sharp delineation between lid and crease (e.g., carving, concealing, or layering contrasting products) to produce a defined cut-crease shape.

vocabulary.label: lower lashline shading
vocabulary.definition: Applying and pressing or sweeping shadow beneath the lower lashes to connect upper and lower color, add balance or definition, distinct from pencil/gel liner.

vocabulary.label: highlight / set bright area
vocabulary.definition: Primarily brightening or setting a high point (e.g., brow bone or inner corner) to clean up, add light, or set product in a concentrated bright area.

vocabulary.label: transition establishment
vocabulary.definition: Creating the initial soft gradient or transition shade (typically in or above the crease) that subsequent colors blend into to build a seamless gradient.

vocabulary.label: lid color placement
vocabulary.definition: Laying down the main lid shade/finish (often by pressing or packing) onto the mobile lid to build core color payoff and coverage.

vocabulary.label: edge diffusion / refinement
vocabulary.definition: Softening borders between shades, blurring harsh lines, and cleaning or refining edges to make gradients seamless and polished.

vocabulary.label: dimension / deepening
vocabulary.definition: Adding depth or contour with darker or more targeted shades to intensify shadow, deepen the crease, or sculpt structure beyond the initial transition.

vocabulary.label: other eye step
vocabulary.definition: Eye-related actions outside the above shadow-construction roles, such as applying liner, lashes, mascara, or grooming brows.

facets.title: Application Wetness
facets.definition: Whether the applicator/product interaction uses added moisture/adhesion aid (dampened brush) versus a dry application mode.
guidelines: Label ‘dampened’ only when the brush is explicitly described/seen as slightly wet/damp to intensify/gloss the shadow.
If product is applied over a tacky base but the brush itself is not dampened, keep as ‘dry’ (this facet is about wetness added at application).
Segment when the demonstrator switches from dry brushwork to damp brushwork (or vice versa).
Use cues: mention of damp brush, visible misting/wetting, or a clear instruction to wet the brush for payoff.

vocabulary.label: dry application
vocabulary.definition: No added moisture or separate adhesive medium is applied during the step — neither the brush nor the target area is intentionally wetted or treated with an adhesive; product is applied in a dry state.

vocabulary.label: dampened brush application
vocabulary.definition: The brush or applicator is explicitly described or shown as slightly wet/damp (e.g., misted or moistened brush) and that dampening is used to intensify colour, sheen, or smooth product laydown; the defining feature is moisture on the applicator itself.

vocabulary.label: adhesive-assisted application
vocabulary.definition: A separate adhesive or tacky medium (e.g., glitter glue, mixing medium, lash adhesive) is used or mixed with the product to improve adhesion or intensity; the adhesion aid, not brush dampness, is the key change to product payoff.

vocabulary.label: misted/spritzed application
vocabulary.definition: The target skin or application surface is intentionally misted or sprayed (e.g., setting spray, water/air flash) before or during product application, adding moisture to the surface and altering finish/payoff while the brush may remain dry.

facets.title: Brush Motion
facets.definition: The primary brush movement pattern used during the step’s main action.
guidelines: Choose the motion that dominates the step: if most time is spent pressing/patting, label as ‘press/pack’ even if a small amount of blending follows.
‘Sweep’ = back-and-forth/windshield-wiper or long strokes; ‘buff’ = small circular/short polishing motions to diffuse; ‘press/pack’ = tapping/pressing to deposit pigment.
Segment when the demonstrator clearly switches from depositing (press/pack) to blending (sweep/buff) as separate contiguous actions, if feasible.

vocabulary.label: sweeping strokes
vocabulary.definition: Back-and-forth, windshield-wiper, or long stroking motions used to move and blend product across a larger area.

vocabulary.label: press / pack
vocabulary.definition: Pressing or patting motions used primarily to deposit pigment or product onto the skin with minimal lateral movement.

vocabulary.label: buffing / polishing
vocabulary.definition: Small circular or short polishing motions used to soften edges, diffuse color, and create smooth transitions without distinct linear direction.

vocabulary.label: precise linear strokes
vocabulary.definition: Single-direction, controlled linear strokes used to draw, outline, or fill with accuracy (e.g., winged liner, lip lining); intended to create a sharp, defined edge rather than to blend.

vocabulary.label: feathering strokes
vocabulary.definition: Short, hair-like directional strokes used to mimic individual hairs or create a soft, elongated shape (commonly used for brow definition or hairlike detailing).

vocabulary.label: smudging strokes
vocabulary.definition: Short, localized back-and-forth or rubbing motions used to blur, soften, or diffuse a defined line or edge to create a smoky or lived-in effect.

vocabulary.label: wiggle/lift strokes
vocabulary.definition: Small back-and-forth wiggle combined with an upward lifting motion (typical of mascara application) used to deposit product while separating and lifting fibers/lashes.

facets.title: Applicator Modality
facets.definition: The main applicator modality used to carry out the step’s core physical manipulation (depositing, blending, drawing, wiping, attaching), grouped by the applicator’s functional form/interface rather than by specific cosmetic product type.
guidelines: Label based on the tool/applicator that performs the primary physical manipulation during the step (the ‘main action driver’).
If multiple tools are used in distinct consecutive actions, segment at the tool change when feasible and label each segment separately.
If a built-in wand/doe-foot/stick is used directly from the container, choose Built-in Applicator even if a brush/finger later refines it (unless the refinement is the core of the step).
Choose Soft Pad/Bud for compressible/absorbent implements used to press, blend, or wipe/clean (including sponges, puffs, cotton pads, and q-tips).
Choose Specialty Device for purpose-built mechanisms whose operation differs from rubbing/painting with a surface (e.g., misting, curling, mascara wand/spoolie use).

vocabulary.label: hands/fingers
vocabulary.definition: Direct application, blending, or manipulation using bare fingertips or the palm/hand as the primary interface for the step’s physical action.

vocabulary.label: soft pad/bud
vocabulary.definition: Compressible or absorbent pad or bud used to press, bounce-blend, smudge, or wipe (e.g., beauty sponge, powder puff, cotton pad, q‑tip) as the main application surface.

vocabulary.label: brush
vocabulary.definition: Bristled brush (face or detail) used to apply, blend, buff, or sculpt product with stroke/rubbing motions as the primary applicator.

vocabulary.label: drawing implement
vocabulary.definition: A rigid or firm-tipped implement used to draw, define, or make precise lines/marks with controlled pressure and direction (e.g., pencil, crayon, felt-tip/pen liner).

vocabulary.label: built-in applicator
vocabulary.definition: An applicator that is integrated into the product packaging and used directly from the container as the primary tool (e.g., doe-foot, tube tip, stick/bullet). If the step’s core action is performed directly with the product’s built-in applicator, label this even when a separate tool later refines the result.

vocabulary.label: specialty device
vocabulary.definition: Purpose-built device or mechanism whose operation differs from simple rubbing/painting with a surface, used as the primary tool (e.g., spray/mist devices, lash curler, standalone electronic tools). Excludes applicators that are integral to the product container (those are labeled Built-in Applicator).

vocabulary.label: accessory placement (no applicator)
vocabulary.definition: Step consists primarily of placing, attaching, or positioning an accessory (e.g., false lashes, stickers, appliqués) rather than applying or blending product with a hand-held applicator.

facets.title: Look Context
facets.definition: Which overall makeup look/occasion the tutorial is currently executing (e.g., daytime wearable vs nighttime dramatic), typically spanning many steps until a clear transition/reset.
guidelines: Label based on the currently active overall look being built, not the specific product being applied in the moment.
Change the label only when the tutorial clearly transitions to a different full look (e.g., after a full removal/reset, or an explicit ‘next look’/‘for nighttime’ switch).
If the video is a single look throughout, keep one label for the whole video.

vocabulary.label: 1920s_day_wearable
vocabulary.definition: The softer, 1920s-inspired daytime wearable segment — vintage/period styling with lower overall intensity (lighter liner, softer eyes/lashes) intended as a distinct historic look.

vocabulary.label: 1920s_night_cabaret
vocabulary.definition: The more dramatic 1920s/cabaret segment — intensified vintage styling (smokier eyes, heavier liner/lashes, bolder overall intensity) intended as a distinct historic evening look.

vocabulary.label: teal_glitter_glam
vocabulary.definition: A bold, colorful glam look centered on teal and glittery/shimmery eye makeup (smoky or accentuated lashes), intended as a statement/night/photo-ready look.

vocabulary.label: dewy_summer_glow
vocabulary.definition: A fresh, glowy/dewy summer look emphasizing luminous skin, light coverage, soft warm color, and an overall radiant, daytime-appropriate finish.

vocabulary.label: daytime_natural_wearable
vocabulary.definition: Everyday/daytime natural or nude look: low-intensity makeup with light coverage, neutral or soft-shimmer lids, subtle/soft liner, natural-looking lashes, and sheer or nude lips, intended for wearable daytime use.

vocabulary.label: nighttime_dramatic_glam
vocabulary.definition: A general intensified evening/night look characterized by deeper/defined complexion, stronger liner or wing, heavier lashes/mascara, and bolder lip/finish — a broad category for non-specific dramatic nighttime transitions.

vocabulary.label: metallic_smoky_glam
vocabulary.definition: A dramatic, nighttime-focused look built around a dark or metallic smoky eye (pressed/damp metallic lid, blended crease, dark waterline) typically paired with understated lips and subtle cheek definition.

vocabulary.label: vibrant_yellow_cut_crease
vocabulary.definition: A bold, editorial/photo-ready eye-focused glam centered on a bright yellow cut-crease (often with cream/gel base and pigmented shadow), sharp graphic liner through the crease, dramatic lashes, and neutral lips.

facets.title: Product Medium
facets.definition: The physical product medium/format being applied or manipulated in the current step, which drives different handling and layering constraints.
guidelines: Label by the primary product medium being actively applied/manipulated in that moment (not secondary products mentioned).
If two media are mixed and applied together as one mixture, label by the mixture’s resulting dominant medium (usually ‘liquid/cream mix’).
If a powder is being pressed into a cream base, label by what is being applied at that moment (cream step vs powder step).

vocabulary.label: powder
vocabulary.definition: Pressed or loose powder products being applied (e.g., powder eyeshadow, powder blush/contour, setting powder); dry particulate medium applied by brush/sponge/pressing and handled differently from creams, liquids, and adhesives.

vocabulary.label: cream_or_liquid
vocabulary.definition: Creamy or pourable liquid emollient products actively being applied or blended (e.g., foundation, concealer, cream base, liquid illuminator/primer mixes); includes pourable or spreadable formulations whose wet/drying behavior governs layering.

vocabulary.label: wax_or_gel
vocabulary.definition: Waxy, gel, or pomade products used for lining, shaping, or defining (e.g., gel liner, pomade-as-liner, brow gels/pomades) with a tackier, malleable medium distinct from powders and pourable creams.

vocabulary.label: solid_stick_lip
vocabulary.definition: Solid stick or bullet-format lip color being applied (traditional lipstick bullet); a solid, molded pigment stick distinct from pencils, balms, or glossy liquids.

vocabulary.label: pencil_or_crayon
vocabulary.definition: Solid pencil or crayon-format products (wooden or retractable cores) with a waxy/creamy core applied by drawing or sketching (e.g., brow pencils, lip liners, kohl); requires precision/sharpening handling unlike powders or pourable creams.

vocabulary.label: spray_mist
vocabulary.definition: Products delivered as an aerosol or pump spray/mist applied as fine droplets across the face (e.g., spray foundations, setting sprays) whose droplet distribution and drying behavior require distinct handling and layering.

vocabulary.label: false_lashes
vocabulary.definition: Preformed strip or individual false-lash assemblies being positioned and adhered to the natural lash line (including adhesive handling and placement/adjustment); treated as an accessory/placement medium rather than a pigment layer.

vocabulary.label: mascara
vocabulary.definition: Brush-wand applied pigmented liquid or cream product dispensed from a tube and applied to coat, lengthen, volumize, or separate eyelashes; handling (wand application, drying) differs from other eye/face products.

vocabulary.label: tinted_balm
vocabulary.definition: Sheer, non-bullet tinted balms or glosses (hydrating/semi-liquid lip products) applied for a light wash of color and moisture; behaves differently from solid stick lip colors and from fully liquid foundations.

vocabulary.label: glitter_with_adhesive
vocabulary.definition: Loose or flaky glitter particles applied as a mixture with a tacky adhesive or gel so the applied medium behaves as an adhesive-borne sparkle layer (e.g., glitter mixed with glitter adhesive), distinct from dry powders or simple pigment layers.

facets.title: Step Function
facets.definition: The primary procedural goal of the current step in the makeup workflow.
guidelines: Choose the dominant functional goal of the step, even if minor secondary effects occur.
If a step explicitly aims to soften edges/smoke out, label ‘diffuse_soften’ even though some pigment is deposited.
If a step is explicitly about reducing/knocking back intensity (blotting, sheering out), label ‘reduce_intensity’.

vocabulary.label: prime_or_prep
vocabulary.definition: Apply products or techniques to condition, smooth, hydrate, or otherwise modify the skin surface so subsequent makeup applies, adheres, photographs, and wears better (primers, moisturizers, balms, pore fillers).

vocabulary.label: map_or_outline
vocabulary.definition: Lightly sketch or mark intended shapes and placement as a guide before applying stronger pigment or committing to the final shape (mapping a cut-crease, outlining brow shape).

vocabulary.label: shape_or_prep
vocabulary.definition: Physically alter or ready a natural feature or area to change its form or improve subsequent product application (curling lashes, pressing or adjusting skin/feature).

vocabulary.label: place_or_build
vocabulary.definition: Lay down product to create or strengthen color, shape, or definition (packing shadow, applying blush/contour/highlighter, applying lipstick) as the primary objective.

vocabulary.label: brighten_or_highlight
vocabulary.definition: Locally increase brightness or illumination of an area to make it appear lighter, more reflective, or lifted (under-eye brightening, baking to lift tone, applying highlight products).

vocabulary.label: increase_intensity
vocabulary.definition: Deliberately amplify color, contrast, or definition to make a feature or the overall look stronger or more dramatic (deeper bronzer, stronger liner, bolder lip).

vocabulary.label: diffuse_or_smoke
vocabulary.definition: Soften, blend, or smudge product to blur edges and create a gradient or smoky effect, prioritizing softened transitions over crisp definition.

vocabulary.label: sharpen_or_define
vocabulary.definition: Create a clean, precise edge or outline—using product, cleanup strokes, or concealer—to crisply define the shape of a feature or correct mistakes.

vocabulary.label: color_correction
vocabulary.definition: Place corrective or neutralizing product specifically to counteract localized discoloration or undesirable undertone (orange/peach under-eye concealer, green corrector for redness) to even the base before layering color/foundation.

vocabulary.label: set_or_lock
vocabulary.definition: Set product in place or merge layers to preserve wear and finish (powder setting, baking, finishing powder) as the primary goal.

vocabulary.label: reduce_intensity
vocabulary.definition: Deliberately tone down intensity, opacity, or shine of product or area (blotting, sheering out, patting to mute) as the main aim.

vocabulary.label: remove_or_reset
vocabulary.definition: Remove product to clean or reset an area (wiping off makeup, removing layers to start again) as the step's primary function.

facets.title: Technique Motion
facets.definition: The dominant physical application/blending motion used in the current step.
guidelines: Label the most repeated/central motion in the step (not a brief supporting motion).
If the step is explicitly about blotting/patting to mute, label ‘tap_or_blot’ even if initial application occurred moments earlier.
If the step is drawing a defined line/wing, label ‘line_or_trace’ even if it is later softened.

vocabulary.label: press_or_pack
vocabulary.definition: Pressing or packing product onto a surface with focused pressure for strong pigment/coverage (e.g., patting shadow or pressing pigment into skin).

vocabulary.label: sweep_or_buff
vocabulary.definition: Sweeping or buffing motions across larger areas to diffuse and blend product for an even, soft finish (e.g., cheek/bronzer sweeps, buffing edges).

vocabulary.label: line_or_trace
vocabulary.definition: Drawing or tracing a defined line or edge with a tip or edge for precision (e.g., eyeliner, lip lining, sharp wing creation).

vocabulary.label: tap_or_blot
vocabulary.definition: Tapping or blotting motions used to lift excess, mute intensity, or gently press product without sweeping (e.g., blotting shine, light tapping to set).

vocabulary.label: place_or_attach
vocabulary.definition: Positioning, placing, and securing external elements or accessories on the face where the dominant motion is placement/adjustment (e.g., applying strip/individual lashes, inserting contacts, setting embellishments).

vocabulary.label: spread_or_smooth
vocabulary.definition: Spreading, rubbing, or smoothing product across the skin using fingers or tools with continuous smoothing strokes to create an even layer (e.g., smoothing primer, creams, moisturizers).

vocabulary.label: brush_or_coat
vocabulary.definition: Brushing, combing, or stroking motions used to coat hairs/fibers or deposit product along hairs (e.g., mascara wand through lashes, brow brush strokes).

vocabulary.label: paint_or_swipe
vocabulary.definition: Gliding or swiping a liquid/creamy applicator across a surface in a continuous stroke to apply color or coverage (e.g., lipstick/gloss swipes, applicator swipes of cream products).

vocabulary.label: wipe_or_swipe
vocabulary.definition: Wiping or swiping motions used to remove, dissolve, or transfer product off the skin with a pad/cloth or applicator (e.g., removing makeup with a cotton pad).

vocabulary.label: smudge_or_blend
vocabulary.definition: Localized rubbing, dragging, or short back-and-forth motions used to soften or blur a defined line or edge into surrounding skin (e.g., smudging eyeliner or shadow for a smoked look).

vocabulary.label: clamp_or_curl
vocabulary.definition: A clamping or squeezing tool motion applied to bend, reshape, or lift an element (e.g., using an eyelash curler to curl lashes).

vocabulary.label: spray_or_mist
vocabulary.definition: Applying product via a spray or fine mist to the face to evenly distribute a lightweight finish (e.g., setting spray, airbrush mist).

vocabulary.label: bounce_or_stipple
vocabulary.definition: Repeated bouncing or stippling taps with a sponge or similar tool to blend foundation/cream products for seamless, natural coverage (e.g., beauty blender stippling).

vocabulary.label: dab_or_dot
vocabulary.definition: Small, precise single or few dabs/dots to place concentrated product in a tiny target area (e.g., inner-corner highlight dotting, targeted concealer placement).

facets.title: Layer Dependency
facets.definition: What pre-existing base/layer the current product application depends on or is being applied over.
guidelines: Label based on the immediate underlying surface at the application site (e.g., cream base on lid, set/powdered skin on cheeks).
If the tutorial explicitly set the area with powder before this step, use ‘over_set_base’ for subsequent cheek/face powders.
For eye steps built on prior shadows/liner (not a dedicated cream base), use ‘over_existing_eye_build’.

vocabulary.label: over_cream_base
vocabulary.definition: Applied on top of a deliberately placed cream primer/base (intended to improve payoff, adhesion, or act as a dedicated base layer) that is the immediate underlying surface.

vocabulary.label: over_set_base
vocabulary.definition: Applied over skin or areas that have been set/finished with powder (a powdered/set complexion) where the immediate underlying surface is the powdered set base.

vocabulary.label: over_unset_liquid_base
vocabulary.definition: Applied on top of freshly applied liquid or cream complexion products (foundation, liquid concealer, or other unset cream/liquid makeup) where that wet/unspecified liquid product is the immediate underlying surface.

vocabulary.label: over_existing_eye_build
vocabulary.definition: Applied on top of a previously built eye makeup structure (earlier shadow, liner or layered eye products) where the earlier eye layers—not a dedicated cream base—are the immediate dependency.

vocabulary.label: over_existing_lip_build
vocabulary.definition: Applied on top of previously applied lip product (lip liner, stain, lipstick, or gloss) where the existing lip product is the immediate underlying surface for edge, adhesion, or color layering.

vocabulary.label: over_existing_brow_build
vocabulary.definition: Applied over previously built brow makeup (filled or painted brows) where the brow product is the immediate underlying layer being worked over or corrected.

vocabulary.label: over_existing_makeup_layer
vocabulary.definition: Applied on top of an earlier makeup product already present at the site (e.g., concealer, powder, pigment, or other prior product) where that prior makeup—rather than a dedicated cream primer or set/powdered skin—is the immediate surface dependency, and no more specific site-based 'existing' label (eye/lip/brow) applies.

vocabulary.label: over_moisturized_skin
vocabulary.definition: Applied atop skin that has been prepped with skincare (moisturizer/serum) but not covered by a dedicated cream primer or other makeup base; the immediate underlying surface is skincare.

vocabulary.label: on_natural_lashes
vocabulary.definition: Applied directly to the wearer’s natural lashes (e.g., mascara applied to native lashes or adhesives applied onto natural lash hairs) where the natural lashes are the immediate surface.

vocabulary.label: over_false_lashes
vocabulary.definition: Applied on or over previously affixed false/strip lashes or products placed when false lashes are already in place (e.g., mascara or glue over attached lashes) where the false lashes are the immediate underlying surface.

vocabulary.label: on_bare_or_fresh_area
vocabulary.definition: Applied directly to a relatively bare or fresh area with no explicit base, skincare, or prior makeup layer described as the immediate dependency at the application site.

facets.title: Application Scope
facets.definition: How large an area is being actively worked during the step (broad multi-zone blending vs one region vs precision detail work).
guidelines: Label by the spatial footprint of the action being performed in that moment, not by the product category.
‘Whole-face/Multi-zone’ includes actions that sweep across multiple face zones (e.g., perimeter + cheeks; setting powder across face).
‘Single region (broad)’ means one main region is covered broadly (e.g., blending shadow across lid/crease; blush across cheeks).
‘Precision detail’ means small, exact placement (e.g., lash line, nose bridge contour, inner corner, brow tail).
Switch labels when the demonstrator clearly moves from broad coverage to precision (or vice versa).

vocabulary.label: whole-face / multi-zone
vocabulary.definition: Application spans multiple distinct face zones or broadly across the face/perimeter in a single step (e.g., setting powder across the face; sweeping bronzer across perimeter and cheeks).

vocabulary.label: single region (broad)
vocabulary.definition: Application covers one main facial region broadly rather than discrete points or fine detail (e.g., blending eyeshadow across lid and crease; applying blush across the cheeks).

vocabulary.label: precision detail
vocabulary.definition: Application confined to a very small, exact facial feature or targeted placement (e.g., along the lash line, inner corner, brow tail, precise nose bridge contour).

vocabulary.label: multiple spot corrections
vocabulary.definition: Application limited to several small, discrete points across the face for targeted correction or brightening (e.g., dotting concealer on multiple blemishes or under-eye brightening dots); distinct from single-region broad coverage and from single-feature precision work.

facets.title: Product Medium
facets.definition: The physical form/consistency of the cosmetic product currently being applied (dry powder vs emollient cream/gel vs liquid vs solid stick/pencil vs mixed).
guidelines: Label based on the product’s form as used in the step (what is actually being applied), not packaging.
If two media are intentionally mixed into one application (e.g., primer + illuminator; foundation mixing), use Mixed/Layered.
If the step is clearly about a pencil/stick application (brow pencil, eyeliner pencil, contour stick), use Solid stick/pencil even if it later gets smudged.
For aerosols/mists, use Liquid/spray.

vocabulary.label: dry powder
vocabulary.definition: Pressed or loose powder products applied dry as particulate material (e.g., eyeshadow, setting powder, bronzer, powdered contour).

vocabulary.label: cream/gel
vocabulary.definition: Emollient cream or gel products applied as a creamy or gel-like film (e.g., cream shadow, cream contour, gel liner).

vocabulary.label: liquid/spray
vocabulary.definition: Flowing liquid products and aerosols/mists used in application (e.g., liquid foundation, concealer, primers, setting sprays, liquid adhesives).

vocabulary.label: solid stick/pencil
vocabulary.definition: Waxy or solid stick and pencil products applied by drawing/dragging (e.g., eyeliner pencil, brow pencil, contour stick, lipstick stick).

vocabulary.label: mixed/layered media
vocabulary.definition: An application that intentionally mixes or combines two or more different product media into one step (e.g., mixing primer + illuminator, layering cream then powder as one combined application).

vocabulary.label: false lash strip
vocabulary.definition: Pre-formed false eyelash bands/strips applied as a solid accessory along the lash line (positioned with adhesive); treated as a distinct product form from powders, creams, liquids, or pencils.

facets.title: Applicator Type
facets.definition: The main applicator/tool in hand that is doing the work in the step (not secondary tools mentioned in passing).
guidelines: Label by the tool that performs the main application/manipulation in the step.
If a step has two tools but one is clearly the key manipulator/finisher (e.g., smudging liner with a cotton bud), label by that key tool.
Face brush vs eye brush: classify by intended use/size and the region being worked (large/medium face brushes vs smaller eye brushes).
Use Cotton tool for cotton pads/buds used for removal, cleanup, or smudging.

vocabulary.label: fingers/hands
vocabulary.definition: Product is applied or blended primarily using the wearer's fingertips or bare hands.

vocabulary.label: face brush
vocabulary.definition: A brush intended for larger face areas (e.g., powder, contour, foundation, fan, duo-fiber) used as the main applicator.

vocabulary.label: eye brush
vocabulary.definition: A smaller brush intended for eye-area application (e.g., shader, blender, small angled liner brush when used as a brush) serving as the main applicator.

vocabulary.label: pencil/pen applicator
vocabulary.definition: A rigid pencil, crayon, felt-tip, or built-in pen-style tip (liner pen, brow pencil, lip crayon/pen) used as the primary applicator.

vocabulary.label: sponge/puff
vocabulary.definition: A larger sponge or powder puff (beauty sponge, cushion sponge, powder puff) used as the main applicator for face products.

vocabulary.label: cotton tool
vocabulary.definition: A cotton pad or cotton bud used primarily for removal, cleanup, or smudging/diffusing in the step.

vocabulary.label: lash tool
vocabulary.definition: Non-brush lash manipulators such as lash curlers, tweezers, or similar tools used as the main tool.

vocabulary.label: wand applicator
vocabulary.definition: A handheld or tube-attached wand-style applicator (e.g., mascara spoolie/brush, gloss doe-foot, small wand brushes) used to coat or deposit product; includes mascara wands and similar spoolie/doe-foot applicators.

vocabulary.label: sponge-tip applicator
vocabulary.definition: A small foam or sponge-tipped applicator (foam eyeshadow tip, smudger tip) used to apply or gently smudge products in small eye areas or along lash lines.

facets.title: Primary Motion
facets.definition: The main physical manipulation pattern used in the step (how the product is moved/placed on skin).
guidelines: Choose the motion that does the primary work (the action that achieves the intended placement/finish).
If a step includes drawing followed immediately by a deliberate diffusion step and that diffusion is the key aim, label Smudge/Diffuse.
Use Sweep/Buff/Blend for circular/back-and-forth blending motions that soften edges or distribute powder.
Use Pat/Press for stamping/packing product to build payoff or set product.
Use Draw/Line for creating a defined line/shape (liner, brow strokes, lip lining).

vocabulary.label: pat/press
vocabulary.definition: Product is stamped, pounced, or pressed onto the skin to deposit or build payoff (packing/pressing motions to set or layer product).

vocabulary.label: sweep/buff/blend
vocabulary.definition: Product is moved with sweeping, circular, or back-and-forth blending motions to soften edges or distribute/blur product across an area.

vocabulary.label: draw/line
vocabulary.definition: Product is applied by drawing a defined line or precise shape with strokes (e.g., liner, brow strokes, lip lining).

vocabulary.label: smudge/diffuse
vocabulary.definition: Product is intentionally smeared or blurred to soften hard edges and create a smoky or diffused effect.

vocabulary.label: spray/mist
vocabulary.definition: Product is applied by spraying or misting a fine aerosol or spray across the face or target area.

vocabulary.label: wipe/remove
vocabulary.definition: Product is removed or cleaned off by wiping, rubbing away, or using a solvent/cleanser to dissolve and lift product.

vocabulary.label: brush/comb
vocabulary.definition: Product is applied, coated, or worked through hairs or across a surface using a bristled tool or wand in directional strokes to deposit, separate, comb, or coat fibers (distinct from circular blending).

vocabulary.label: place/adhere
vocabulary.definition: A discrete object (lash strip, contact lens, adhesive element) is positioned, aligned, and set onto the skin or target area, with precise placement and adhesion as the primary action.

vocabulary.label: swipe/glide
vocabulary.definition: Product is applied by swiping or gliding an applicator or product across a surface in one or repeated linear passes to deposit an even film.

vocabulary.label: smooth/spread
vocabulary.definition: Product is smoothed or spread across the skin using fingers, a flat tool, or a paddle-like applicator to create an even thin layer (distinct from blending circularly).

vocabulary.label: paint/fill
vocabulary.definition: Product is applied to fill in an area to build continuous, opaque coverage (outlining and then filling an area or painting on solid color).

facets.title: Active Feature
facets.definition: Which facial feature/region is the primary focus of the current step (the area being actively worked on).
guidelines: Label based on the main area being actively manipulated during the step (where product is being placed/blended).
If multiple areas are mentioned, choose the area that receives the primary action/time; if truly balanced, choose the area that imposes the stricter constraints (usually eyes over complexion).
Keep the same label across consecutive steps that remain on the same region; switch when the tutorial clearly moves to a different region (e.g., finishes base and begins eyes).

vocabulary.label: complexion_base
vocabulary.definition: Base skin work across the face (primer, concealer, foundation, color-correcting, setting powder) where the goal is creating/adjusting the complexion.

vocabulary.label: cheeks_highpoints
vocabulary.definition: Cheek-area products and placement on cheekbones and nearby high points (blush, bronzer, cheek highlighter, temples) intended to shape or add color/highlight to the cheek area.

vocabulary.label: eyes
vocabulary.definition: Any work on the eye area (lid, crease, brow bone, inner corner, eyeliner, waterline) including color placement, blending, liner application, and eye-focused shading.

vocabulary.label: brows
vocabulary.definition: Eyebrow grooming, shaping, filling, or setting actions focused specifically on the brows.

vocabulary.label: lashes
vocabulary.definition: Eyelash-specific actions such as curling, applying mascara, lash serums, or attaching false lashes.

vocabulary.label: lips
vocabulary.definition: General lip product application or definition (full-lip color, lining, balm, gloss) targeting the lips as a whole.

vocabulary.label: nose
vocabulary.definition: Work targeted to the nose (bridge, sides, tip) such as contouring, highlighting, powdering, or sculpting to define nose shape.

vocabulary.label: cupid_bow
vocabulary.definition: Precise highlighting or definition of the cupid's bow area above the upper lip (spot highlight or shaping) distinct from full-lip application.

vocabulary.label: full_face
vocabulary.definition: Actions that target the entire face as a unit unrelated to a specific base product category (e.g., full-face cleansing, makeup removal/reset, or treatments applied to the whole face).

facets.title: Eye Placement
facets.definition: For steps involving the eyes, which eye sub-region/surface is the primary placement target; non-eye steps are labeled explicitly as such.
guidelines: If the step does not work on the eye area, label as non_eye.
If waterline/tightlining is included at any point in the step, label as waterline_mucosa (it dominates constraints).
Otherwise label by the primary placement: eye_contour_skin for brow bone/inner corner/lid; lashline_skin for liner along the lash line without waterline.
Change label when the demonstrated placement switches to a different eye surface (e.g., lid blending → waterline tightline).

vocabulary.label: non_eye
vocabulary.definition: The step does not primarily target the eye region (no placement on eye-area skin, lashes, mucosa, or ocular surface).

vocabulary.label: eye_contour_skin
vocabulary.definition: Placement on the external skin of the eye area (brow bone, inner corner, eyelid surface, crease) — does not include working the waterline/mucosa, eyelash hairs, or eyebrow hairs.

vocabulary.label: lashline_skin
vocabulary.definition: Placement along the lash line on skin (upper or lower lash line), e.g., applying eyeliner to the skin at the base of the lashes — excludes work on the waterline mucosa or on the lash hairs themselves.

vocabulary.label: waterline_mucosa
vocabulary.definition: Placement on the waterline or tightline (the mucosal surface of the eyelid), including upper waterline tightlining. When present, this label takes precedence over other eye placements in the same step.

vocabulary.label: eyelashes
vocabulary.definition: Placement or actions directed at the eyelash hairs themselves (e.g., curling, applying mascara/primer, coating/combing lashes, attaching or manipulating false-lash bands) where the lash shafts/band are the primary target rather than adjacent skin or mucosa.

vocabulary.label: brow_hair
vocabulary.definition: Placement or actions targeting the eyebrow hairs (filling, shaping, tinting, waxing/setting of brow hairs) as the primary target, distinct from the skin of the brow bone.

vocabulary.label: ocular_surface
vocabulary.definition: Placement on the exposed ocular surface (the visible eye/cornea), e.g., inserting or placing contact lenses or other actions that contact the eye surface itself — distinct from waterline mucosa and external skin.

facets.title: Complexion Layer
facets.definition: For complexion work, the functional layer-step within the base routine; non-complexion steps are labeled explicitly.
guidelines: If the step is not about complexion/base products, label non_complexion.
For complexion steps: choose the label matching the step’s functional role (prep/prime, correct/conceal, foundation, set).
Use surrounding sequence cues: primer typically precedes concealer/foundation; powder setting typically follows; touch-ups later in a look are labeled touch_up_refresh.
Switch labels at clear transitions in the base routine (e.g., concealer → foundation, foundation → powder).

vocabulary.label: non_complexion
vocabulary.definition: A step that is not part of the complexion/base layering routine (examples: eyes, brows, lashes, lips, or other non-face-base work).

vocabulary.label: prep_prime
vocabulary.definition: Base preparation intended to improve skin texture, hydration, or product wear before coverage layers (e.g., moisturizers, primers, skin prep).

vocabulary.label: correct_conceal
vocabulary.definition: Targeted correction and concealing to neutralize localized discoloration, dark circles, or spots prior to or around foundation application.

vocabulary.label: foundation_even_out
vocabulary.definition: Applying a foundation or tinted base across broader areas of the face to even overall complexion and create an initial uniform coverage layer.

vocabulary.label: set_lock_in
vocabulary.definition: Setting complexion layers—typically with powders or setting sprays—to reduce shine/transfer and lock coverage in place.

vocabulary.label: touch_up_refresh
vocabulary.definition: Later reapplication or refreshing of complexion coverage and re-setting after wear (touch-ups performed during a look or before intensifying the makeup).

vocabulary.label: contour_sculpt
vocabulary.definition: Applying contour products (cream or powder) to create shadow and definition on facial planes (cheeks, nose, jawline, hairline) as a sculpting step distinct from general foundation or setting.

vocabulary.label: highlight_illuminate
vocabulary.definition: Applying luminizing or highlighting products to high points or small accents (cheekbones, nose, brow bone, inner eye) to add targeted brightness, glow, or perceived lift on top of the base.

vocabulary.label: blush_add_color
vocabulary.definition: Applying cheek color (blush) to introduce a flush, tint, or warmth focused on the apples/center of the cheeks to balance and finish the complexion.

vocabulary.label: bronze_add_dimension
vocabulary.definition: Applying bronzer to warm and subtly sculpt the face—typically on the perimeter, temples, and cheeks—to create a sun-kissed, dimensional finish distinct from blush or contour shading.

facets.title: Look theme/era
facets.definition: Which broad styling theme or era the current look segment is aiming to match (e.g., explicitly 1920s-inspired vs not period-specific).
guidelines: Assign based on the currently active overall look the tutorial is building; keep constant across multiple steps until the creator clearly switches to a different look/segment (often via explicit announcement or remove/reset).
Use explicit cues like “1920s,” “flapper,” “cabaret,” or period references to label the segment as 1920s-inspired; otherwise label as contemporary/unspecified.
Do not infer theme/era from a single product shade (e.g., teal) unless the tutorial frames it as part of a period look.

vocabulary.label: 1920s-inspired
vocabulary.definition: The tutorial segment is explicitly framed as drawing from the 1920s era or associated styles (e.g., flapper, cabaret, or other period-specific references); includes day or night variants when the creator signals a 1920s/period look.

vocabulary.label: contemporary-or-unspecified
vocabulary.definition: The tutorial segment is not explicitly tied to a historical period; includes modern everyday, modern glam, colorful/editorial, or otherwise unspecified contemporary looks (covers any non–period-specific styling).

facets.title: Look intensity/occasion
facets.definition: The intended overall intensity and wear context of the current look segment (e.g., daytime wearable vs nighttime glam vs statement/editorial).
guidelines: Label based on how the creator frames the whole look segment (e.g., ‘daytime,’ ‘wearable,’ ‘night out,’ ‘dramatic,’ ‘editorial,’ ‘photo-ready’), not on a single momentary step.
Keep the label stable across the segment; change only at clear look switches (explicit announcement, reset/removal, or a sustained pivot in goal such as ‘let’s make it nighttime’).
When in doubt between nighttime-glam and statement/editorial: use statement/editorial only when the tutorial frames the goal as especially bold/graphic/photo-focused beyond typical ‘night out’ glam.

vocabulary.label: daytime-wearable
vocabulary.definition: Lower-to-moderate intensity looks intended for everyday or daytime wear — lighter coverage, softer definition, and an overall more natural or casual finish. Use when the creator frames the segment as daytime, work/casual wear, or explicitly ‘wearable’.

vocabulary.label: nighttime-glam
vocabulary.definition: Higher-intensity looks intended for evening or night occasions — stronger definition, deeper color payoff, more dramatic eyes/contour/lashes typical of night-out or party makeup. Use when the creator frames the goal as evening, night out, or explicitly ‘glam’.

vocabulary.label: statement-editorial
vocabulary.definition: Deliberately bold, graphic, or highly saturated looks meant to stand out on camera or as a creative statement (editorial/photo-ready). Use when the creator frames the segment as especially bold/graphic or for photos/editorial purposes beyond typical night-out glam.

facets.title: Application Region
facets.definition: Which main facial region is being actively worked on during the step (where the product is being applied/adjusted).
guidelines: Label by the primary region receiving application/adjustment during the step; ignore secondary incidental contact (e.g., holding skin taut).
Switch labels when the demonstrator clearly transitions to working on a different region (e.g., finishes eye work and begins lips).
If a step truly spans multiple regions as a single combined action, use 'multi-area/other' (otherwise choose the dominant region).

vocabulary.label: eyes
vocabulary.definition: Primary work on eyelids, lash lines, waterline, or nearby eye detailing (shadow, liner, eye primer, tightlining, etc.). Secondary/incidental contact with other areas is ignored.

vocabulary.label: lips
vocabulary.definition: Primary work on the lip perimeter or lip surface, including lining, filling, or application/adjustment of lip products.

vocabulary.label: complexion/face
vocabulary.definition: Primary work on skin or base-face areas such as primer, foundation, concealer, powder, blush, bronzer, and highlight—i.e., overall complexion work.

vocabulary.label: brows/lashes
vocabulary.definition: Primary work on eyebrows or eyelashes, including shaping, filling, tinting, applying brow products, mascara, lash application, or curling.

vocabulary.label: multi-area/other
vocabulary.definition: Steps that genuinely span multiple facial regions as a single combined action, or that pertain to an area outside the main face regions (e.g., contacts), where no single region clearly dominates.

facets.title: Linework Geometry
facets.definition: The primary line/outline shape being constructed during the step, considering where and how the line extends.
guidelines: Only use the specific geometry labels when the main action is drawing/placing a line or outline; otherwise label 'not a linework step'.
Choose based on the dominant intended shape (e.g., any explicit outward flick/extension from the lash line counts as a wing).
Switch labels when the demonstrator stops one linework type and begins a different one (e.g., lashline liner then separate graphic crease line).

vocabulary.label: winged upper liner
vocabulary.definition: Upper lashline liner drawn along the upper lashes that extends outward past the outer corner into a distinct wing or flick.

vocabulary.label: upper lashline (no wing)
vocabulary.definition: Liner or definition placed along the upper lashline without an outward wing extension; an external line that follows the lash roots.

vocabulary.label: upper waterline (tightline)
vocabulary.definition: Product applied directly to the inner rim/upper waterline (tightlining) between the upper lashes to darken the base of the lashes rather than creating an external lashline stroke.

vocabulary.label: lower waterline
vocabulary.definition: Eyeliner applied to the inner rim of the lower eyelid (the lower waterline) on the inner lash rim to darken or define the inner lower lash area (distinct from product placed beneath the lashes).

vocabulary.label: lower lashline
vocabulary.definition: A line or band of product placed along or just beneath the lower lashes (external lower lash area), including crisp or smudged/smoky applications intended to define the lower lashline (distinct from waterline application).

vocabulary.label: graphic eye line (non-lashline)
vocabulary.definition: A deliberate drawn line on the eye area that is not primarily along the lashline (for example, a graphic crease line, inner-corner graphic extension, or inward-pointing liner); used when the main action is drawing a non-lashline graphic shape.

vocabulary.label: brow outline
vocabulary.definition: A drawn or traced line that defines or reinforces the perimeter/shape of the eyebrow (arch and tail), created with pencil, brush, shadow, or by shaping with concealer; used when the primary action is outlining the brow edge.

vocabulary.label: lip outline
vocabulary.definition: A line drawn to trace or shape the lip perimeter (lip lining) to define the lip edge.

vocabulary.label: not a linework step
vocabulary.definition: The step’s primary action is not drawing an outline or line (for example: blending shadow, applying base products, lashes, brushing, or other non-linework actions).

facets.title: Edge Finish Intent
facets.definition: Whether the step is intended to leave edges crisp/sharp or intentionally softened/diffused, versus making no explicit edge-finish change.
guidelines: Label 'softened/smudged' when the step includes purposeful blurring, smudging, or diffusing an edge as a key intention.
Label 'crisp/sharp' when the step emphasizes clean lines, sharpness, precision, or refining/cleaning edges.
Label 'no explicit edge finishing' when the step is mainly placement/deposit without an explicit goal of sharpening or diffusing edges.
Switch labels when the demonstrator transitions from placing product to a distinct edge-finishing phase (e.g., draw line → smudge; place shadow → blend edges).

vocabulary.label: crisp/sharp edge
vocabulary.definition: Step's primary intent is to create, refine, or emphasize a clean, defined boundary or line (drawing, sharpening, or cleaning edges for precision).

vocabulary.label: softened/smudged edge
vocabulary.definition: Step's primary intent is to blur, smudge, diffuse, or blend an edge to make it appear softer, smokier, or more lived-in.

vocabulary.label: no explicit edge finishing
vocabulary.definition: Step focuses on product placement or general application without a distinct action aimed at either sharpening or diffusing edges.

facets.title: Eye Look Type
facets.definition: The overarching eye-look construction style being built in the surrounding portion of the routine, inferred from preceding/following eye steps (shadow placement/blending, finishes like glitter, and overall intensity).
guidelines: Assign based on the broader eye segment cues: cut-crease mapping/carving/graphic lines → 'cut-crease/graphic'; heavy blending/smoky gradients and/or glitter emphasis → 'smoky/glitter'; single soft wash/very subtle definition → 'minimal/soft'.

Use 'not an eye-look step' for steps primarily about lips, complexion, brows, lashes (unless the tutorial segment is explicitly about eye-look construction and the action directly changes the eye look).
Change labels at clear routine boundaries (e.g., daytime portion vs evening intensification in a day-to-night tutorial).

vocabulary.label: cut-crease/graphic eye
vocabulary.definition: Eye look defined by a sharp cut-crease or graphic liner/shape that creates clear separations or precise edges between lid and crease (carving, concealing, or graphic lines).

vocabulary.label: smoky/glitter eye
vocabulary.definition: Eye look built from blended, smoky gradients emphasizing depth and diffusion and/or the use of glitter/metallic finishes to add shimmer or sparkle.

vocabulary.label: minimal/soft eye
vocabulary.definition: Subtle, daytime-oriented eye look with a single soft wash or very light definition, minimal shadow complexity, and no pronounced graphic or heavy smoky construction.

vocabulary.label: not an eye-look step
vocabulary.definition: Step does not materially build or change the eye look (primarily concerns lips, complexion, brows, lashes when not altering the eye construction, or non–eye-related actions).

facets.title: Eye Application Operation
facets.definition: The dominant operational mode being performed on the eye area during a contiguous segment, characterized by the primary goal of the step and the typical hand/brush action used to achieve it.
guidelines: Label by the single dominant operation for the segment; if the demonstrator clearly switches operations (e.g., pack → blend), split into separate segments when feasible.
Prefer the operation that occupies most time/attention or is explicitly stated as the purpose (e.g., “to deepen” vs “to blend out”).
Do not label by the specific product/shade; label by what is being done to the eye (prepare, blend, pack, deepen, carve, refine/smudge, define lines/hairs, lashes/mascara).
If an action is primarily cleaning/sharpening/softening borders (even using the same shade), choose Refining/Softening rather than the earlier placement operation.
If a step is explicitly carving a lid shape with concealer/product to create a sharp boundary, choose Cut-Crease/Carving even if minor blending follows.
If the action is attaching lashes or coating lashes with mascara, choose Lash Work regardless of any small cleanup around it.

vocabulary.label: prep / map base
vocabulary.definition: Preparing the eye surface and mapping initial placement to guide later work (primer/base application, light sketching or placement to set up shape and adhesion). This is an initial preparation operation rather than color-building or shaping.

vocabulary.label: blend transition / gradient build
vocabulary.definition: Creating or expanding a soft gradient (typically in the crease/upper crease) using blending motions to diffuse edges and establish seamless transition between shades.

vocabulary.label: pack / place lid color
vocabulary.definition: Depositing the main lid color or finish on the mobile lid using pressing/packing/placement motions to build coverage and payoff (distinct from blending or creating transition).

vocabulary.label: deepen / sculpt dimension
vocabulary.definition: Adding targeted depth or contour (e.g., outer corner, crease depth) to intensify structure, typically with concentrated application and controlled strokes to deepen the area.

vocabulary.label: cut-crease / carve shape
vocabulary.definition: Carving or reinforcing a sharp lid–crease boundary (often with concealer or a contrasting product) to create a defined cut-crease shape; chosen when the explicit purpose is to create a crisp boundary even if minor blending follows.

vocabulary.label: refine / diffuse / smudge edges
vocabulary.definition: Softening, cleaning, or perfecting borders and lines—edge diffusion, smoothing transitions, or smudging a defined edge to achieve a softer or tidier finish rather than adding new color depth.

vocabulary.label: define lines or hairs
vocabulary.definition: Creating precise definition with controlled strokes (eyeliner, tightlining, brow/hairlike detailing) where the goal is a defined mark or hair-like line rather than blended coverage.

vocabulary.label: lash work
vocabulary.definition: Working directly on lashes as the primary operation — applying mascara (including wiggling/lifting motions), attaching false lashes, or otherwise coating/placing lashes.

vocabulary.label: highlight / brighten
vocabulary.definition: Applying a lighter, luminous or brightening product to lift and illuminate specific eye-area points (e.g., inner corner, brow bone, adjacent high points). Typically done with precise placement/tapping to add highlight rather than to build depth or blend transitions.
