dataset.title: Makeup Tutorial | Smokey Eye Makeup Look + Face & Lips | TheMakeupChair

transcript.text: Apply an eyeshadow primer evenly across the entire eyelid to create an even base and help shadows adhere and last. If you don’t have an eyeshadow primer, use concealer over the lid instead as the base.

While the primer is still slightly tacky, sweep a matte eyeshadow close to your skin tone through and just above the crease, blending upward toward the brow bone. This sets the base so later shades blend more smoothly.

Using a fluffy blending brush, apply a warm crease/transition shade directly into the crease with back-and-forth motions. Build it gradually and blend well, then lightly pull the same shade down onto the lid to begin the smokey gradient and create a base for the darker/metallic shade.

With a flat brush that’s slightly damp, press the smokey (darker/metallic) shade onto the lid. Focus on the center first, then work it across the lid, blending down and outward while keeping most intensity on the lid area.

Pick up a small amount of the lid shade on a blending brush and lightly buff around the edges of the darker color to diffuse harsh lines. Keep pressure light and continue blending until the transition looks smooth and smokey.

Repeat the same process on the second eye: press the smokey metallic shade onto the lid (a damp brush helps it glide and look glossier), then go back in with the blending brush to soften and blur any harsh lines for symmetry.
Use a soft matte shade (similar to the blush tone you’ll wear) as a final blending/transition color. Sweep it through the crease to create a subtle fade that helps the smokey eye look more seamless.
Apply a slightly lighter shadow to the inner corner/tear-duct area to brighten the eyes and add dimension, tying the smokey tones together.
Apply black eyeliner to the upper and lower waterline to intensify the smokey effect and deepen the eye look.
Using the flat brush, pick up a small amount of the smokey lid shade and press/sweep it underneath the lower lashes to add definition and connect the upper and lower shadow.
Apply plenty of mascara (including the lower lashes as shown) to add volume and length and complete the smokey eye.
Lightly tap off excess product and apply a small amount of the same ‘fade shade’ onto the cheeks as blush, helping balance the face and harmonize with the eye look.
Outline the lips with a lip liner (she uses a brow liner as a substitute) to define shape and prep for lipstick.
Apply a nude-toned liquid lipstick to the lips to keep them understated so they don’t compete with the dramatic smokey eyes.

Using a brow brush and dark brown eyeshadow, fill in the eyebrows and sketch a thin, elongated brow shape. Extend the tail so the brow line reaches toward the outer corner/end of the eye for a more 1920s-inspired shape.
Build more shadow through the brows (and brush through if needed) to make them look thicker and more diffused, avoiding a harsh ‘penciled-in’ look.
Apply concealer around the edges of the brows to sharpen the shape and correct any mistakes, creating a clean outline.
Apply a light orangey-brown matte eyeshadow across the entire eyelid, blending it upward so the color reaches toward/near the eyebrow for that vintage, lifted wash of color.
Using a medium brown from the same palette, add definition in the crease and blend it so the color comes about halfway across the eyelid, creating soft dimension.
Line the upper lash line with a thin amount of eyeliner for subtle definition (kept light for the daytime/wearable version).
Use an eyelash curler to curl the upper lashes to open the eyes and prepare for mascara.
Apply mascara to the upper lashes, coating and lifting them for definition without overpowering the soft shadow.
Apply concealer under the eyes to brighten the area before adding any lower-lash-line product; blend to smooth and even out the under-eye tone.
Use a light brown eyeshadow to create a soft shadow along the lower lash line, adding gentle definition without harsh lines.
Apply a very light amount of mascara to the lower lashes so they stay natural and balanced with the softer daytime eye.
Add a small amount of blush to the cheeks to warm up the complexion, keeping placement soft and wearable.
Apply highlighter to the brow bone and the tops of the cheekbones to add a subtle glow and lift to the face.
Apply a red lipstick, then lightly pat/blot it to mute the intensity and create a more toned-down, wearable red lip finish.
Use a makeup remover on a cotton pad to dissolve and wipe away the makeup (including waterproof products) without hard scrubbing, cleaning the face so you can start the next look fresh.
Redo the eyebrows using the same brow technique/shape from the first look so the brow style matches while the eye/lip become more dramatic.
Press brightening/setting powder under the eyes to protect the skin and make it easier to clean up dark eyeshadow fallout while building the smoky eye.
Apply a pinky-gold eyeshadow into the crease and build it up to a heavier intensity, creating a warm retro base for the deeper shades.
Pack an eggplant-purple eyeshadow across the entire eyelid to create the main dramatic color for the night/cabaret-style eye.
Apply a thicker line of eyeliner along the upper lash line, then smudge it to soften and smoke out the edge; embrace slight imperfection for a sultry effect.
Repeat the thick, smudged eyeliner effect along the lower lash line to balance the upper lid and intensify the smoky eye.
Use the same purple eyeshadow to smudge into/over the eyeliner, further diffusing the edges and deepening the smokiness around the eyes.
Apply strip lashes along the upper lash line and adjust them into place so they sit comfortably and enhance the dramatic eye.
Apply mascara to the top lashes, then apply a heavier amount to the bottom lashes to emphasize the lower lash line for a bold, cabaret-inspired finish.
Apply a small hint of blush, then highlight the brow bone and cheekbones again to complement the dramatic eyes while keeping the complexion lifted and luminous.
Finish with an opaque, bright red lipstick application for a classic 1920s-inspired bold lip that pairs with the smoky eyes.

dataset.title: Nude Makeup | Easy Everyday Makeup Tutorial | Indian Skin | corallista

transcript.text: Begin the base by applying a slightly orange-toned liquid concealer to areas of darkness and discoloration. Dot it under the eyes, around the nose, and around the mouth (and optionally on the eyelids if you have pigmentation). Blend the concealer out seamlessly using a brush to diffuse the edges and even the complexion before foundation.

Apply a thin layer of liquid foundation over the face to lightly even out the skin without looking heavy. Use a face brush to blend across the cheeks, chin, and the rest of the face, keeping coverage light for a natural, nude finish.

Set the concealer and foundation using a pressed/compact powder. Sweep on a very light layer with a fluffy face brush to lock the base in place, help it last longer, and control excess oil (especially through the T-zone).
Apply a natural, matte blush to the cheeks to add a subtle hint of warmth without strong color payoff. Blend it into the cheek area so it looks soft and natural on the skin.

Using an eyeshadow quad, pick the lightest shade and apply it under the brow bone and in the inner corner of the eyes to brighten. Lightly dust the same shade along the tops of the cheekbones to add a soft glow while keeping the look nude.
Apply the second shade (a soft gold) all over the eyelid to give a sheer, subtle shine. Blend evenly across the lid for a light, natural shimmer suitable for an everyday nude look.
Use the darkest shade (soft bronze) from the quad to add definition. Smudge it along the upper lash line and the lower lash line to softly deepen the eyes without creating a harsh, dramatic effect.

Apply a soft black kajal very close to the upper lash line, keeping the line thin. Use a sponge-tip applicator to gently smudge the kajal so it looks softer and less harsh. Then apply kajal along the upper waterline (tightlining) to make lashes look fuller.

Curl the eyelashes first with an eyelash curler. Then apply mascara to lengthen and volumize while keeping the lashes separated and natural-looking; coat the upper lashes and then apply to the lower lashes as well for a balanced, defined nude-eye finish.
Complete the look by applying a tinted lip balm (sheer brown tint) directly to the lips. Build a light, even layer for a natural-looking wash of color that complements the nude makeup.

dataset.title: Day to Night Makeup Tutorial for Indian skin | corallista

transcript.text: Apply a makeup primer to help the base last longer and reduce foundation breakdown from skin oils. If you have dry skin with only an oily T‑zone, concentrate primer on the T‑zone; if you’re oily overall, spread it across the entire face. Pat/smooth it in with fingertips, focusing on areas that get oily (around nose, under-eyes/cheeks, center of face).

Use a slightly orange-toned concealer/corrector before foundation to neutralize darkness. Dot product under the eyes and around areas of discoloration such as the sides of the nose and around the mouth, then blend out evenly (using a brush) so the correction looks seamless and doesn’t leave harsh edges.

Choose a long-lasting foundation for day-to-night wear. If your foundation is a bit light, mix it with a slightly deeper shade to match your skin tone. Apply and buff/blend over the face (starting around the center like the nose/cheeks and working outward) until coverage looks even and natural.

Set foundation and concealer with a matte/setting powder to lock the base in place and reduce shine. Press/sweep powder over the face, paying extra attention to areas that tend to get oily (forehead, nose, chin).

For a daytime look, keep cheek products soft: apply blush to add healthy color, then use only a small amount of highlighter for a gentle glow. Optionally, use the highlighter on the brow bone and the inner corners of the eyes to brighten the eye area without looking overly intense.

Apply a brown eyeliner along the upper lash line for a softer daytime definition. Immediately smudge the liner slightly (using a cotton bud) to diffuse the edge and create a subtle, lived-in line rather than a sharp stripe.

Curl eyelashes to lift them, then apply mascara for a natural daytime finish. Use the lighter/subtler mascara wand option first (the side that picks up less product) to keep lashes defined but not too dramatic.

Apply a long-lasting matte lip stain/lipstick in a wearable nude/pink-brown shade. Use the applicator to coat lips evenly and let it dry down from a brief glossiness to a matte finish, completing the daytime makeup.

Before intensifying for evening, refresh the complexion: reapply a small amount of concealer where it has worn off (e.g., under-eyes or around the nose/mouth) and blend. Then set again with powder to lock the touch-up in place and remove any excess oil/shine.

Use face palette products to increase definition for night. Apply bronzing powder to add warmth and structure (e.g., around cheek area), then add a bit more highlighter than in the daytime to create a stronger glow on the high points of the face.
Switch to black liquid eyeliner for a more dramatic evening eye. Draw a winged liner along the upper lash line, extending outward to form a clean wing for added intensity.
After liner, reapply mascara for a fuller evening effect. Use the mascara wand option that deposits more product (the more dramatic side) to add extra volume and impact.

Finish the day-to-night transformation by applying a bright red long-wear lip stain. Use the applicator to outline and fill in the lips carefully, building an even, opaque red for an evening-appropriate pop of color.

dataset.title: TEAL GLITTER SMOKEY EYE (requested by Jaclyn Hill!) | PatrickStarrr

transcript.text: Apply Nivea Aftershave Balm all over the face (especially after shaving) to moisturize and act as a primer base before complexion products.

Dot Marc Jacobs Remarkable foundation (shade Honey Deep) onto the face (forehead, cheeks, chin) using a small amount since it’s very pigmented, then blend out evenly with a duo-fiber brush for full coverage.
Lightly mist/apply Dior Air Flash over the base to neutralize excess yellow and improve the overall tone while keeping the finish you like.
Apply Urban Decay concealer to conceal (under eyes and other areas as needed). Add Benefit Shy Beam on top to further brighten the under-eye/highlighted areas.
Use a Morphe G2 brush to blend all concealer and Shy Beam seamlessly into the foundation until the edges disappear.
Using the Anastasia medium cream contour kit, mix/use the shades Cinnamon and Chocolate to softly contour (cheek area and perimeter), keeping it blended (no harsh/streaky lines).
Press Laura Mercier powder under the eyes to set/brighten (baking), then use Airspun powder around the rest of the face to set the base. Leave the under-eye powder looking bright while it sets.
With a Sigma E40 blending brush, sweep Anastasia Burnt Orange through the crease as the main transition shade. Build intensity gradually and blend thoroughly until the transition looks smooth.
Use Anastasia shade ‘Buttery’ on a Morphe M433 brush to highlight under the brow arch/brow bone and soften the top edge of the crease work.
Buff Makeup Geek ‘Morocco’ into the crease slightly lower than the first transition to add warmth and dimension; blend to keep the gradient smooth.
Apply Makeup Geek ‘Americano’ into the crease to create a soft, dark-chocolate cut-crease effect. Keep it blended so the crease is defined but not harsh.
Apply ColourPop cream gel ‘Zulu’ (seafoam/pastel green) across the eyelid as a base to help the teal lid color appear brighter and more opaque.
Press Makeup Geek ‘Dragonfly’ (teal) on top of the cream base across the lid to create the teal lid color, building coverage to an even, saturated finish.

Mix Makeup Geek glitters (Solstice and Martian) with Lit Cosmetics glitter adhesive, then pat the mixture over the eyelid to create a bright teal glitter finish (using more Solstice for a lighter teal).
Draw a bold black winged liner along the upper lash line, extending and shaping the wing to match the smoky/glitter eye. Refine until both sides look clean and sharp.
Curl natural lashes, then apply a first strip lash (New Bouncin’ ‘Bellas’). Once tacky/set, stack a second lash (Lilly Lashes ‘Doha’) on top for extra drama, adjusting placement with tweezers.
Sweep Makeup Geek ‘Morocco’ along the lower lash line to create a smoky base, then smudge ‘Americano’ closer to the lashes to deepen and intensify the lower lash smoke.
Use ColourPop gel liner ‘Swerve’ to line the bottom waterline with black for added intensity and definition.
Coat the bottom lashes with Extend-A-Plate mascara to define and lengthen after smoking out the lower lash line and lining the waterline.
Use Makeup Forever Pro Finish Powder to dust over the face, blending everything together and knocking back/remove the heavy bake/setting powder look for a smooth finish.
With MAC Mineralize Skinfinish (Dark Deep) and a Morphe M527 brush, add powder contour to sculpt the cheeks/outer face for more definition over the set base.
Using the same contour powder (Dark Deep), contour the nose with an e.l.f. fan brush to ‘snatch’/define the bridge and shape.
Apply The Balm ‘Mary Lou Manizer’ to highlight the nose and cupid’s bow (skipping cheek highlight to keep attention on the eyes).
Sweep Tarte Amazonian Clay Blush in ‘Captivating’ across the cheeks for warmth and color while keeping the overall look balanced with the bold eye.
Use Benefit Browsing: apply the brow powder toward the front of the brows for a softer start, then use the wax toward the tail/outer brow to define and set the shape.
Line lips with MAC ‘World’ lip liner, apply LipLand Cream Corset lipstick, then top with Anastasia ‘Undressed’ gloss to create a nude, glossy lip that complements the teal glitter smoky eye.

dataset.title: Makeup Tutorial Philippines: Easy Glowy Summer MakeUp Tutorial for 2018 by Dianne | BeKami

transcript.text: Prep the skin for a dewy summer finish by moisturizing, then applying a luminous primer (Burberry Fresh Glow Nude Radiance #01) mixed with a liquid illuminator (Liquid Glow in Peach Fizz). Spread and blend the mix evenly over the face with fingers for an all-over glow.

Use a small amount of foundation (Fenty Beauty Pro Filt’r Foundation, shade 300) for lighter coverage. Dispense a little product and blend it out across the face (shown blending with a sponge/beauty blender) to even the complexion while keeping the look fresh and glowy.

Apply concealer (Tarte Shape Tape Concealer, shade Medium) to areas needing extra coverage/brightening (e.g., under eyes and other spots), then blend thoroughly so the edges melt seamlessly into the foundation.

Set the foundation/concealer using Kat Von D Lock-It Setting Powder. Press/pounce the powder onto the skin with a beauty sponge to lock makeup in place, while explicitly avoiding baking to keep the base more natural and glowy.
Add warmth and soft dimension by bronzing with Anastasia Beverly Hills Bronzer in Rich Amber, focusing on typical bronzing areas (around the perimeter/cheek area) to enhance a sun-kissed look.

Apply a warm eyeshadow shade for summer color using an Anastasia Beverly Hills Eyeshadow Single in “Sunset.” Blend it onto the eyelids/crease area to add soft warmth without making the eye look too heavy.
For a less-intense, softer liner, use Anastasia Beverly Hills Dipbrow Pomade in Dark Brown as eyeliner. Apply along the lash line to define the eyes while keeping the overall look subtle.
Coat the lashes with Maybelline Hypercurl Mascara to lift and define, emphasizing the eyes without overpowering the soft, summery eye look.

Define the lips with a lip liner from Zitomer Pharmacy in the shade “Sienna.” Trace and shape the lip line (and lightly fill if needed) to create a base that helps the lip color last and look more defined.

Layer a glossy lip product over the liner for a glowy finish, using Anastasia Beverly Hills Lip Gloss in the shade “Bronzed.” Apply evenly to add shine and a warm tone that complements the summer look.
Use Anastasia Beverly Hills x Amrezy Highlighter to brighten the inner corners of the eyes (and add small luminous touches as desired) to enhance the overall glow and make the eyes look more awake.
Add a healthy flush using an Anastasia Beverly Hills Blush Trio—selecting one shade and sweeping it onto the cheeks. Blend to a natural, sun-warmed finish to complete the glowy summer complexion.
